topics.title: Social issues and trends
topics.content:
Students must study the themes and sub-themes below in relation to Poland. Students must study
the themes and sub-themes using a range of sources, including material from online media.

children.title: Theme: Aspects of Polish-speaking society: past and current trends
Sub-theme: The Polish family
children.content:
- Changing roles within the family
- The generation gap
- Traditional and modern values

children.title: Sub-theme: The evolution of the digital world in Poland
children.content:
- The internet in daily life
- Social media – benefits and dangers
- The digitalisation of Polish society

children.title: Theme: Aspects of Polish-speaking society: past and current issues
Sub-theme: Social diversity and mobility in Poland
children.content:
- Education and career choices
- People on the margins of society
- Tolerance and respect

children.title: Sub-theme: Impact of emigration on Polish society
children.content:
- Reasons for emigration
- Advantages and disadvantages for Polish society
- Attitudes within Poland to migration

topics.title: Political and artistic culture
topics.content:
Students must study the themes and sub-themes below in relation to Poland. Students must study
the themes and sub-themes using a range of sources, including material from online media.

children.title: Theme: Artistic culture in the Polish-speaking world past and present
Sub-theme: Festivals and traditions
children.content:
- Roots and origins
- Social and economic impact
- Regional and local heritage

children.title: Sub-theme: Polish cultural life
children.content:
- Cinema
- Art
- Music

children.title: Theme: Aspects of political life in Poland past and present
Sub-theme: Poland and the European Union
children.content:
- The role of Poland in Europe
- The benefits of membership of the EU for Poland
- The challenges of membership of the EU for Poland

children.title: Sub-theme: Polish politics and young people
children.content:
- Young people and their engagement with politics
- Priorities for youth politics in Poland
- Values and ideals

topics.title: Grammar
topics.content:
A-level students will be expected to have studied the grammatical system and structures of the
language during their course. Knowledge of the grammar and structures specified for GCSE is
assumed.
In the exam students will be required to use, actively and accurately, grammar and structures
appropriate to the tasks set, drawn from the following lists. The mention of an item in these lists
implies knowledge of both its forms and its functions at an appropriate level of accuracy and
complexity.
The examples in italics in parentheses are indicative; they serve to illustrate the part of speech or
structure that the student must know and do not represent an exhaustive specification of the
required grammatical knowledge.

children.title: Nouns
children.content:
Gender: masculine, feminine, neuter
Singular and plural forms
Declension/cases: nominative, accusative, genitive, dative, ablative/instrumental, locative/vocative
Agreement

children.title: Pronouns
children.content:
Declensions
Personal (eg Kto? Co?)
Demonstrative (eg Który? ten, ta, to, tamten, ci, te, tamci, tamte)
Possessive (eg Czyj? mój, twój, jego, jej, nasz, wasz, ich, swój)
Numeral (eg Ile? kilka, dużo, wiele, mało)
Reflexive (eg się, sobie, siebie, z sobą)
Forms of address (eg ty, pan, pani)

children.title: Adjectives
children.content:
Gender
Agreement
Declension
Comparative (eg ładniejszy, bardziej mokry)
Superlative (eg najładniejszy, najbardziej mokry)
Demonstrative (eg ten kolor jest ładny/ta dziewczyna jest smutna/to dziecko jest wesołe)
Interrogative (eg Który? Która? Które?)
Possessive (eg Czyj? Czyja? Czyje?)

children.title: Adverbs
children.content:
Comparison (eg bardziej radośnie/mniej poważnie/nieco wolniej)
Interrogative (eg Jak się masz?/Kiedy będą wybory?/Gdzie są moje okulary?)

children.title: Verbs
children.content:
Infinitive
Tenses: present, past and future
Aspects: imperfective, perfective (eg czytałem, przeczytałem)
Impersonal forms (eg często mówiono o tym/zadano mi pytanie)
Negative forms (eg nie odrobiłem zadania domowego/nie wiem o co chodzi)
Interrogative forms (eg Zapłacił pan mandat? Była pani u lekarza?)
Indicative (eg czytam)
Imperative (eg czytaj! czytajcie!); imperative/subjunctive (eg Niech pani przeczyta.)
Conditional (eg czytałbym/abym)
Participles: adverbial present (eg czekaj ą c), adverbial past (eg wziąwszy)
Adjectival present (eg czekaj ą cy)
Adjectival passive (eg napisany)
Active voice (eg Mama myje syna.)
Passive voice (eg Syn jest myty.)
Reflexive verbs (eg Syn się myje.)
Prefixes as a grammatical/lexical amendment to some of the verb forms as exemplified above:
zaczytałem się, oczytana, umyty, wymyty,

children.title: Indirect/direct speech
children.content:
(eg Idę grać z kolegami w piłkę – powiedział Paweł./Paweł powiedział, że idzie grać z kolegami w
piłkę.)

children.title: Conjunctions
children.content: (eg a, albo, ale, by, i, jeżeli, gdy, aby, ani, czyli, ponieważ, kiedy, lub, że, żeby, chociaż, gdyby)

children.title: Numbers
children.content:
Cardinal
Ordinal
Indefinite (eg Wiele gatunków zwierząt wymarło w tym okresie./Dałam tylko trochę soli do zupy.)
Collective (eg dwoje, troje)
Fractions (eg pół, ćwierć, trzy czwarte)

children.title: Syntax
children.content:
Flexibility of word order depending on semantic emphasis (eg Ładny jest ten kolor. ale To dziecko
jest wesołe.)

Andrzejewski: Popiół i diament

children.content:
Katyń: Andrzej Wajda (2007)
Przypadek: Krzysztof Kieślowski (1981)

topics.title: Research project
topics.content:
Students will choose one of the research topics below and must cover all the bullet points in their
research.

children.title: Research topic: Poland during the communist era
children.content:
- Impact on daily life
- Influence of the Catholic Church
- The Solidarity movement

children.title: Research topic: Racism in Poland
children.content:
- Origins of racism
- Victims of racism
- The fight against racism

children.title: Research topic: Tourism in Poland
children.content:
- The development of a tourist infrastructure
- Popular tourist sites/places of interest
- Regional gastronomy

children.title: Research topic: The resistance movement in Poland during World War II
children.content:
- Resistance organisations
- Forms of resistance
- Actions and operations
